thesis: A lava lamp is slow, warm, hypnotic: wax that is heated at the bottom swells, lets go, drifts up, cools, sags back down; the whole object is a heat engine you can watch.
job: open the page and see a lamp glowing in a dim room
watch blobs rise, stretch, pinch off, merge, sink
switch the lamp off and on; see wax cool and settle, then warm and wake
change heat and see the speed and size of blobs change
poke or stir the wax with the pointer
reset / leave it running as ambient

principles: wax is slightly denser than liquid when cool, slightly lighter when hot
bulb heats bottom, top is cooler
surface tension pulls blobs round and merges them
tricks: per-blob temperature rather than a global force
tests: do blobs ever stall forever at the top or bottom
does it feel slow like honey not bouncy

principles: sum of radial falloff fields, threshold gives iso-surface
tricks: soft alpha band at threshold for antialias
shade by field value for inner glow
bottom pool as a wide static blob row
tests: blobs pinch off with a neck, not overlap circles

principles: glow is the subject, room is dark
tricks: metal cap and base with gradient banding
tests: can a stranger name it a lava lamp at a glance

principles: controls are real buttons and sliders

kinds.name: classic glass-and-base lamp, canvas metaballs
kinds.what: tapered capsule on a metal base, coloured wax in liquid

descriptions: base widens, cap narrower than glass top
behaviors: blobs stretch vertically when moving fast

descriptions: wax lighter and hotter at bottom
behaviors: off lamp is dim and desaturated
heat off: all blobs cool, sink, pool
heat up: pool bulges, blobs detach again
status text shows warm/cool and temperature

anti_keywords.instead: dark room lit by the lamp itself
every control changes heat, colour or motion

checks: Would a stranger say lava lamp at a glance?
Do blobs merge, neck and detach?
Does power off cool and settle the wax, and on warm it again?
Does every control change visible state?
Works at phone width with no external requests?
